I’ll trace how server-info is routed and add dedicated capacity while preserving its response and public access behavior.
I’m using the repository’s Python style skill. The endpoint currently runs through the Flask-to-ASGI bridge, which shares a thread limit with other requests. I’ll give its two routes a separate limit in that bridge so they retain the existing Flask response and authentication behavior.
The bridge can reserve capacity without duplicating the endpoint handler. I also found that basic auth still required authentication for server-info despite marking it public for authorization. I’m adding an exact-path exemption for both API paths, including the configured static prefix.
The 28 focused tests passed, covering exhausted shared capacity, identical response bytes, and unauthenticated access on both paths with and without a static prefix. Pytest then hit a sandbox permission error in the repository’s process-reporting hook after the tests completed.
Implemented dedicated worker capacity for both server-info paths, so shared-pool exhaustion no longer blocks capability discovery.

The existing Flask handler remains unchanged, preserving response content and Gunicorn/Waitress compatibility. Both paths are publicly accessible with custom static prefixes.

All 28 focused tests passed. Pytest’s post-test reporting hook then encountered a sandbox permission error. No dependencies were installed.
